pr_title: Add support for homekit_controller secondary entities like power usage
pr_body: ## Proposed change A HomeKit bridge is composed of accessories. Accessories are composed of services. Services are composed of characteristics. (A single accessory follows the same structure but only has a single accessory). The initial model of homekit_controller was to create an entity per service and to link services within the same accessory with the device registry. We are starting to hit the limits of that model. Entities like a TV are compromised of multiple services. There isn't a "primary service" to hang off of with a HomeKit camera. And there are a bunch of cases where we actually need to create multiple entities from a single service. This is the first in a series of PR's to break the existing assumption. Later PR's will rationalise and simplify the existing code. The original mechanism is still supported but now in addition there are hooks in place to load a platform if a particular characteristic is detected and to allow a platform to register a callback for creating characteristic entities. To demonstrate how these entities will look we add support for 2 vendor specific characteristics for real time energy usage monitoring, finally fixing #27220. (Nothing currently plugged in, hence 0W). ## Type of change - [ ] Dependency upgrade - [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New integration (thank you!) - [x] New feature (which adds functionality to an existing integration) - [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break) - [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests ## Example entry for `configuration.yaml`: N/A ## Additional information - This PR fixes or closes issue: fixes #27220 - This PR is related to issue: - Link to documentation pull request: ## Checklist - [x] The code change is tested and works locally. - [x] Local tests pass. **Your PR cannot be merged unless tests pass** - [x] There is no commented out code in this PR. - [x] I have followed the [development checklist][dev-checklist] - [x] The code has been formatted using Black (`black --fast homeassistant tests`) - [x] Tests have been added to verify that the new code works. The integration reached or maintains the following [Integration Quality Scale][quality-scale]: - [x] No score or internal - [ ] 🥈 Silver - [ ] 🥇 Gold - [ ] 🏆 Platinum To help with the load of incoming pull requests: - [x] I have reviewed two other [open pull requests][prs] in this repository. pr_comments: Note that the uncovered lines in this were uncovered before, they just moved. Theres no new uncovered code.

I _think_ this will also allow, for example, [the iSmartGate](https://ismartgate.com) when paired to `homekit_controller`<sup>1</sup> to correctly have multiple cover entities exposed corresponding to multiple underlying services. (IIRC I also ran into this with multi-outlet HomeKit power strips that expose each controllable outlet as a service).

Thanks for your work here. Happy to help if needed.

<sup>1</sup> though to be fair this specific example isn't as 'urgent' of a win now that the [`gogogate2` integration also supports iSmartGate devices](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/gogogate2/).

Hard to say without seeing the JSON created in .storage/homekit_controller-entity-map when you pair with those devices.

This PR is for the case where you have an outlet service and then vendor specific sensor characteristics on the side like a power usage sensor. Or a humidifier which has a separate vendor specific numeric setting for the mist level. It could help if you had some sort of on/off characteristic multiple times within a single service. But that would be a very very unusual device. I don't think it would work in iOS, so it's unlikely that a certified bought-in-a-shop device would do it.

I believe 2 outlet services or 2 covers within a single accessory should work already. They have different service iid's, the common problem is where you have 2 accessories with the same serial number and same iid. Please file an issue if your devices don't fall into this category (along with the JSON data I mentioned) and I can see why the device isn't enumerated properly.

Thank you for your contributions.

comments: Hey there @Jc2k, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`homekit_controller`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L129) for? Thanks!

Thanks for raising this ticket. I have Koogeek light strip working with Home Assistant so hopefully we can figure out what is wrong with your smart plug.

I'm not sure what AP mode is - I have assumed it is "Access Point" mode. If not please ignore those points.

You have made a few different points and some of them may or may not be related, for example if HA can't see the plug when in AP mode - that is expected. If it can't see it when you have it paired with Apple Home - that is also expected. If it can't see it after you have done a hard reset of the device itself - that is also expected. But there are other cases when its not. So we need to construct a timeline of what you try and in what order and what happens.

When pairing with Home Assistant the device should not be in access point mode (if thats what AP mode is). And it should not be paired with your apple devices.

The normal pairing flow for a Koogeek device seems to be:

 * to first pair it with HomeKit on an iOS device. This will get it to be a wifi client on your network
 * to then unpair it from within the Home app. But do not do a hard reset on the device itself. The device should remain on your wifi but no longer appear in your Home app as paired.
 * at this stage as a debugging step you can optionally use your router admin to find the devices ip address and verify it is still on the network by pinging it.
 * at this point the device should appear in Home Assistant. If not you could try restarting Home Assistant. If still not, then try disconnecting power from the Koogeek and connecting it again. Give it a minute.
 * If it's still not showing at this stage, try waiting. mDNS is over UDP and unreliable, some users have had trouble with the packets arriving due to weak wifi signals.
 * If it's still not working, try monitoring mDNS on your home assistant box. Something like `tcpdump -i eth0 udp port 5353` where `eth0` is the interface that you are using as your primary gateway. Try restarting the KooGeek again. You should see tcpdump events as the Koogeek announces itself on your wifi. If you don't then you have a network problem.
 * If you get to the stage where you can enter a pairing code, make sure you include the dashes when entering the PIN code. The Koogeek will reject the cryptographic handshake if you don't put the dashes in.

When paired, future communication is over TCP and the protocol is less reliant on mDNS, so hopefully if you do have reliability issues they will be greatly reduced after pairing is complete.

If you are still having trouble after following these steps then can you give a timeline of what you tried as bullet points. Try to capture as much information as possible. We don't have access to your device, your HA instance or your network setup so we only have what you tell us to go on. Ideally try and monitor your Koogeek starting with mDNS as described ^ as this can rule out networking issues quickly.

mDNS (the mechanism used for discovery) may not be fully functional depending on your network setup. So please also include details of your network. Do you have vlans? Do you have one flat subnet for wifi and ethernet? Or are there 2 subnets? What brand of networking gear do you use?

I do not use HASSIO myself, i use Home Assistant directly. And i only ever run it in a custom Docker container or from the command line of my development machine. So all the logs I look at are on stdout. I can't help you find where they are for your particular environment, unfortunately.
Also, if you get HA errors in the UI please include the text or a screenshot. There are many errors, and knowing exactly which one you see is very helpful
